title: 8051/MCS-51: CPU, memory, and peripherals

spans.text: The 8051, also called MCS-51, is an 8-bit microcontroller family. The classic core combines a CPU, program and data memory spaces, timers, serial communication, interrupts, and four 8-bit I/O ports. Many modern chips are compatible derivatives, not identical copies: memory sizes, clocking, peripherals, and timing must be checked in the exact device datasheet.

IMPORTANT REGISTERS

A (accumulator) is the main operand for many arithmetic and logic instructions; B supports operations such as multiply and divide. R0–R7 are working registers in one of four selectable banks. PSW holds flags and the bank-select bits. DPTR is a 16-bit data pointer, SP tracks the stack, and PC holds the next instruction address. Special Function Registers (SFRs) expose control registers and I/O ports at defined addresses.

MEMORY AND I/O

The architecture distinguishes code memory from data memory. MOVC reads a byte from code space; MOVX accesses external data space on devices that implement it. Internal RAM, bit-addressable locations, register banks, and SFRs have distinct roles and address rules. P0–P3 are byte-wide ports on the classic device; P0 has open-drain behavior and normally needs external pull-ups when used as general-purpose I/O. Consult the part's pin and electrical specifications before connecting a load.

spans.title: Check the exact chip
spans.text: The original 8051 has well-known memory and timing characteristics, but compatible derivatives vary. Do not copy memory sizes, vector tables, port electrical assumptions, or machine-cycle calculations without checking the target datasheet.
